originality.rationale: Frieswijk et al. 2022 derive the analyzed planar differential equations and establish endemic equilibria, local stability, and sufficient conditions for cycles, but the inspected exact ODE, theorem statements, and proof do not give a periodic invariant-measure identity linking protection variance, covariance, and mean epidemic burden. The present relation imposes a strict mean-prevalence excess at any finite oscillation amplitude. Other inspected epidemic behavior frameworks use different state equations. Published mean–variance shell findings for other nonlinear flows use a similar method but not a theorem implying this model-specific infection premium. One closely relevant 2023 SIS/game paper was accessible only through a bibliographic abstract and is retained as a substantive residual risk.
residual_risks: The 2023 Paarporn–Eksin SIS/evolutionary social distancing paper is conceptually close; its full text could not be obtained, and a covering theorem is not ruled out by an abstract.
A generic invariant-measure identity may have been worked out independently under other terminology; the indexed and literature searches are not exhaustive.

The stated result uses a general averaging method, so novelty is limited to the particular explicit model-specific variance shell and strict oscillatory epidemic-burden comparison, not the method or cycle existence.
No independent expert audit, literature certification or independent validation has occurred.

value.rationale: The paper already proves an oscillatory regime, but not whether cycling self-protection causes higher or lower *mean* infection than the internal endemic equilibrium, nor how that difference scales with protective-behavior variance. The exact strictly signed nonlinear penalty provides a waveform-independent epidemiological invariant at arbitrary amplitude, and the negative covariance is a structural signature of feedback. This directly answers a motivated model-specific burden question rather than an arbitrary small-case computation or a restatement of the existing attractor theorem.
